reports.title: James Quinton
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

promises.quote: 1. The Emergency Department has considered the use of scribes in the course of resuscitation within the emergency department. The Matron, has discussed this with the Care Group Educator and work has commenced on training individuals as scribes in such situations and to ensure that observations are accurately collated and recorded in the course of the
promises.summary: Implement scribes and improve observation charting

promises.quote: a working group has been set up with representation from ED and Anaesthetics to explore further the issue of IV drug administration in emergencies during resuscitation. The first meeting is scheduled for the end of April to look at systems and processes for working together within the Resus area.
promises.summary: Establish working group for IV drug administration

promises.quote: The first meeting is scheduled for the end of April to look at systems and processes for working together within the Resus area.

concerns.quote: During the course of the evidence it became clear that the poor quality nursing notes and the lack of information of the observation chart made it difficult for the reviewing Consultants to get a clear picture of events that had been occurring. Clearly poor record keeping has significant implications for patients.
concerns.hazard: poor quality nursing notes and lack of observation chart information

concerns.quote: 2) Furthermore, during the course of the resuscitation a decision was made for Mr Quinton to be given 4 mgs of Noradreneline. This was to be given as an infusion. Unfortunately, this was actually given as a 4 mg iv bolus. Although the records suggest this did not have a detrimental effect on Mr Quinton (his blood pressure had been exceptionally low) this clearly could be highly significant for other patients. It also raises the question of other patients being given either the wrong drug or the
concerns.hazard: wrong drug or wrong amount or wrong method of administration

concerns.quote: It would seem sensible to have some checking procedure by the person administering the drugs checking with the person who had prescribed it to make sure their understanding is correct. From the evidence | heard it seems there are no such procedures in place.
concerns.hazard: absence of checking procedure for drug administration

reports.title: Robert Fuller: Prevention of future deaths report
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

promises.quote: We have taken the opportunity to review and refine our Enhanced Care Policy and this is proceeding through our governance process for sign off over the coming weeks. One of the changes has been to separate our Falls Risk Assessment and Confusion Risk Assessment to support easier recognition of patients who are either a falls risk or those patients who need a designated level of supervision due to behaviours of concern.
promises.summary: Review and refine Enhanced Care Policy to separate risk assessments

concerns.quote: There was evidence of poor record keeping on the ward. This included behaviour charts, enhanced patient supervision records and daily evaluation charts not being consistently recorded. There was either no or poor documentation of other professionals entering the ward and evaluating patients, and the outcome of such assessments not being recorded. Some of the documentation was also described as not fit for purpose within the frailty unit due to the needs of the patients. This insufficient record
concerns.hazard: inadequate documentation of patient behaviour and assessments
